File: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh
Line or code reference: 265-295 (single_pass_open_followups)
Problem: The function counts all open pipeline-authored security issues that reference the branch, without verifying if those issues contain the required finding IDs from the current audit.
Why it fails at runtime: An older open security issue from a previous audit cycle on the same branch will be counted, causing the gate to incorrectly emit awaiting_followups and suppress the critical alert, even if the current audit's new findings have no corresponding follow-up issue.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh
Line or code reference: 270 (gh api call inside single_pass_open_followups)
Problem: The function does not handle potential API rate limits or transient failures beyond the fail-open return of 1. If the API call fails or times out, the gate treats it as followups_unverifiable and holds the merge, which is safe, but it does not differentiate between a truly missing follow-up and a transient failure.
Why it fails at runtime: A transient API failure during follow-up correlation could repeatedly stall a PR until the stale threshold is hit, adding unnecessary delay.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
TASK_GAP
Requirement: The review-blocked judge (PR comment entry[11], 2026-10-06T13:30:13Z) ordered a fix for the follow-up correlation defect: "the new follow-up check does not establish that the current audit's findings have follow-ups. One older open security issue for the same branch makes the gate emit `awaiting_followups`, silencing the CRITICAL alert even if a newly reported finding has no issue." The judge-fix commit message (d10d041, "Preserve the current audit's finding IDs...") spells out the exact change required:
1. `scripts/security_audit.sh:1963-1992` already has the IDs when creating follow-ups; pass them through the audit summary consumed by `.github/workflows/security-audit.yml:315-323`.
2. Include them in the `findings` report at `scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:594-605`.
3. At `scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:260-295,382-429`, use the cached PR comments to obtain the IDs from the latest pipeline-authored findings report for this head and cycle.
4. Treat missing or malformed IDs as `followups_unverifiable`.
5. Count only open issues from the pipeline account on this branch whose `<!-- ai:security-finding:<id> -->` markers cover every reported ID; otherwise emit `followups_missing`, not `awaiting_followups`.
Expected change site: `scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh` (the `single_pass_open_followups` function at lines 260-295, the `single_pass_marker` function at lines 130-133, and the findings-report path at lines 594-605); `scripts/security_audit.sh` (the follow-up creation block around line 1963 and the audit summary path); `.github/workflows/security-audit.yml` (lines 315-323, audit summary hand-off).
Evidence of absence: The judge-fix commit d10d041 changed only `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` and `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` (removing `invocation.config_override` from a commit check — a separate guard fix for a different CI failure, unrelated to the blocker the judge cited). No diff hunk in any of the four required sites implements the finding-ID correlation. The `single_pass_open_followups` function at `scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:265-295` still counts any open `ai:security` issue whose body contains `Integration branch: <ref>` matching the PR head ref — it does not parse the issue's `<!-- ai:security-finding:<id> -->` markers or check them against the current audit's finding IDs. The `single_pass_marker` at `scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:130-133` still emits only `status`, `head`, `cycle` with no finding IDs. The PR comment entry[3] confirms the live marker format: `<!-- ai:single-issue-security-pass:v1 status=findings head=6cdd8b6f232e0bc37def12eeaa88c85eac1b7aa9 cycle=1 -->` — no finding IDs. Because `single_pass_open_followups` continues to count only branch-name matches, an older open security issue from a prior cycle for the same branch satisfies the check, the gate emits `awaiting_followups`, and `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:6761-6764` (the new `security_hold_awaiting_followups)` case) suppresses the Telegram alert entirely. The 24-hour `followups_stalled` escalation does not fire because the findings marker's `created_at` is fresh. The judge-suppression behaviour the PR ships in this very diff therefore leaves the original bug in place: a current audit's newly reported finding without a follow-up issue will not page a human.
SEVERITY: BLOCKER
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

HARDENING_SUGGESTION:
File: scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh
Location: single_pass_marker (lines 130-133) and single_pass_open_followups (lines 265-295)
Issue: The marker carries no finding IDs and the follow-up counter does not cross-reference them, so the `awaiting_followups` branch silently emits a hold-reason that the Telegram step treats as self-resolving even when the open follow-up issues are stale or unrelated to the current cycle.
Suggested minimal fix: Add finding IDs to the marker (`<!-- ai:single-issue-security-pass:v1 status=%s head=%s cycle=%s findings=%s -->`), then have `single_pass_open_followups` parse each candidate issue body for `<!-- ai:security-finding:<id> -->` markers and intersect that set with the IDs from the latest findings marker; return a per-id status (covered / missing / unverifiable) so the gate can pick the right reason. Without that, the BLOCKER task gap cannot be closed.
Estimated lines changed: ~25 (marker + jq filter + tests)
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
